# Tolerance monotone across laws

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`tolerance-monotone-across-laws` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](tolerance-monotone-across-laws.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> For the same waits and the same start, a formation giving under a tolerating law gives under every law tolerating at least as much, at every step: a law keeping inclusion into another keeps it along their courses.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. One law keeps inclusion into another where, from configurations within others, it gives only where the other does; it then keeps it along their courses, keeping inclusion its case. (`Becoming.Tolerance.KeepsInclusionInto`, `Becoming.Tolerance.KeepsInclusionInto.course`)
2. The tolerating law keeps inclusion into the tolerating law of tolerances no smaller, so more tolerance gives no less at every step. (`Becoming.Tolerance.tolerating_into`, `Becoming.Tolerance.tolerating_mono`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; tolerances and waits given; any start.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That more tolerance is better: only that it gives no less.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
